--- title: "Single-trial estimates" subtitle: "Estimate trial-wise betas with the public single-trial and beta APIs." jupyter: python3 execute: freeze: auto --- A standard GLM gives you one beta per *condition*. Many analyses — representational similarity, trial-wise decoding, single-trial variability — instead need one beta per *trial*. That is what single-trial estimation produces. The entry point is `estimate_single_trial(...)`: pass a time-by-voxel response matrix and a time-by-trial design, choose a method, and get back a `SingleTrialResult` with one estimate per trial per voxel. (`fmrimod.betas` holds older beta-extraction wrappers; new code should use `estimate_single_trial`.) ## A Trial-wise Design The example uses eight separated trial regressors with a known amplitude gradient. Voxel 1 receives the full gradient, voxel 2 receives half, and voxel 3 is null. ::: {#9ca26b4d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd from fmrimod.betas import estimate_betas from fmrimod.single import estimate_single_trial rng = np.random.default_rng(21) n_time, n_trials, n_voxels = 90, 8, 3 X = np.zeros((n_time, n_trials)) for trial, onset in enumerate(np.arange(8, 72, 8)): X[onset:onset + 3, trial] = [0.2, 1.0, 0.4] truth = np.linspace(0.5, 2.0, n_trials)[:, None] * np.array([[1.0, 0.5, 0.0]]) Y = X @ truth + rng.normal(scale=0.03, size=(n_time, n_voxels)) ``` ::: ## LSS Through the Dispatcher `method="lss"` is *least-squares separate*: it fits one model per trial, each with that trial's own regressor plus a single regressor collapsing all the other trials. This keeps the per-trial estimates from being destabilized by the heavy collinearity between closely spaced trial regressors — the reason you cannot just read trial betas off one big least-squares fit. `estimate_single_trial` selects the estimator by the `method` argument and carries trial labels (and standard errors, when requested) through to the result. ::: {#23f40769 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} labels = [f"trial_{i + 1}" for i in range(n_trials)] result = estimate_single_trial( Y, X, method="lss", return_se=True, trial_labels=labels, ) type(result).__name__, result.method.value, result.betas.shape, result.se.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ('SingleTrialResult', 'lss', (8, 3), (8, 3)) ``` ::: ::: The recovered beta series tracks the injected amplitude gradient trial-by-trial — the test that the estimator is actually recovering per-trial signal, not just returning an array of the right shape. ::: {#540e146f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} pd.DataFrame({ "trial": labels, "truth_voxel_1": truth[:, 0], "estimated_voxel_1": result.betas[:, 0], }).round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
trial truth_voxel_1 estimated_voxel_1
0 trial_1 0.500 0.544
1 trial_2 0.714 0.760
2 trial_3 0.929 0.934
3 trial_4 1.143 1.159
4 trial_5 1.357 1.373
5 trial_6 1.571 1.542
6 trial_7 1.786 1.774
7 trial_8 2.000 2.004
``` ::: ::: ## Compatibility Beta Extraction `estimate_betas` is the beta-oriented compatibility entry point for older code. It returns the same LSS estimates in a smaller `BetaResult`; the dispatcher adds the richer metadata you usually want in new analyses. ::: {#fea0e7cf .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} beta_result = estimate_betas(X, Y, method="lss", trial_labels=labels) pd.Series({ "max_abs_delta": np.max(np.abs(beta_result.betas - result.betas)), "compat_method": beta_result.method, "preferred_result": type(result).__name__, }) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` max_abs_delta 0.0 compat_method SingleTrialMethod.LSS preferred_result SingleTrialResult dtype: object ``` ::: ::: Use `estimate_single_trial` when you want labels, standard errors, whitening metadata, or method-specific diagnostics carried with the trial betas. ## Next - [Linear model](linear-model.qmd) - [Sketched and AR-aware models](sketched-ar-models.qmd)
